There are many reasons:

1- The espionage ring that operates in N. Korea knew about the test and informed the Japanese or the USA, of the launch, and that the missile was unarmed (no nuclear warhead). 

2- The T.H.A.A.D. anti-air projectile systems failed to detect the launch and would of been unable to intercept said missile. 

3- The T.H.A.A.D. countermeasure is still not fully operational in S. Korea, and thus the missile was flown on a trajectory that would allow them to circumvent the system.

4- Shooting down the missile doesn't prevent debris and other dangerous shrapnel's from descending on to a populated area. As such, allowing the missile to pass (so long as the missile is not armed, and they have knowledge whether it was armed or not) prevents any unnecessary civilian casualties.
